subject: humanities
passage: Before printing, every copy of a book was made by hand, and each scribe introduced errors of his own, so that no two manuscripts of a long text were identical. Historian Gérard Lemaire argues that the printing press, introduced in Europe in the mid-fifteenth century, changed this by fixing texts. Once type was set, hundreds of copies could be pulled from it in the time a scribe needed for one, and readers in distant cities could, for the first time, cite the same words on the same page.
passage_b: Printing did make it possible to produce many copies far faster than any scribe could. But early printed editions were less uniform than they appear. Printers routinely corrected errors while a sheet was being run, without discarding the sheets already printed, and then bound corrected and uncorrected sheets together. Surviving copies of a single edition, such as Shakespeare's First Folio of 1623, therefore often differ from one another. The stability we associate with print was a slow achievement of later practice, not an immediate effect of the press.
stem: Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?

choices.A: Copies of a single early printed edition were usually identical to one another.
choices.B: Early printers seldom corrected errors once a book's type had been set.
choices.C: Printing allowed copies of a book to be produced far more quickly than by hand.
choices.D: The stability of printed texts developed gradually through later printing practices.

explanation.why: Text 1 says hundreds of copies could be printed "in the time a scribe needed for one." Text 2 agrees that printing made it possible "to produce many copies far faster than any scribe could." The authors disagree about whether early print fixed texts, but both accept that printing was much faster than hand copying.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 1 implies this, but Text 2 says copies of one edition "often differ from one another."
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 says printers "routinely corrected errors" during a print run.
explanation.C: Correct. Both texts state that printing produced copies much faster than scribes could.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is Text 2's view; Text 1 presents fixed texts as an effect of the press itself.
